key_insight: Pac-Man agent failures require separate checks of perception and decision-making: accurate static screenshot reading does not guarantee reliable interaction, and further policy optimization can worsen action choices.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate perception during use, validate full-game performance separately from training success, and inspect decisions across checkpoints before deploying an agent.
method: Studied a Qwen3.5-9B-based agent using only up, down, left, and right actions.
Ran separate perception checks and primitive-policy reinforcement-learning studies.
Used textual boards in the policy study to remove image transcription from the decision interface.
evidence_signal: On eight held-out mazes with three extra lives, completion rose from 0% before policy optimization to 80.2% at a selected checkpoint.
watch_item: The selected-checkpoint result on textual boards should not be treated as evidence of equally reliable end-to-end visual gameplay.
paper_title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man
